newsitem.title: USA: CSX deal strong, US corporate bond spreads steady.
newsitem.headline: CSX deal strong, US corporate bond spreads steady.

text.p: Strong dealer demand for CSX Corp's $2.25 billion issue at attractive levels prompted some investors that had been sidelined to reenter the corporate market on Thursday, dealers said.
Secondary spreads were mostly unchanged, meanwhile, as prices rose with U.S. Treasuries, they added.

The CSX deal was either issue bid or issue plus bid in the Street at when formally priced at mid-afternoon, traders said. Separately, junk rated paper also performed well with a $240 million Allied Waste Industries Inc zero coupon issue trading up more than two points when freed.

Back in high-grades, traders said the the CSX deal adrenalized the secondary market in early goings with some previously coy investors coming off the sidelines. At the same time, they stressed just as many accounts were still cautious ahead of the release of April jobs data on Friday and that dealers were responsible for strongest bidding.
"The (CSX) deal says there's a lot of cash (with investors) and they are being opportunistic as to when they want to it work," said one trader away from the selling group.

Some market participants said the relatively slow market dictated that CSX and other deals were priced to sell. In a better market, one without as much interest rate uncertainty, 30-year bonds for a "solid railroad credit" may have priced as tight as 95 basis points over the Treasury curve, according to one industrials trader.
Many tranches priced at the tight side of price talk. The
deal included:
--$350 million five-year debt at a 53 basis point spread.
--$300 million seven-year debt at a 63 basis point spread.
--$450 million 10-year debt at a 78 basis point spread.
--$400 million 20-year debt at a 95 basis point spread.
--$500 million 30-year debt at a 104 basis point spread.
--$250 million 30-year debt with a put option in the eighth
year at a 60 basis point spread.
The deal also included two privately placed tranches totaling $250 million, bringing the grand total to $2.5 billion, market sources said.

Other high-grade issuance included $250 million Baa1/BBB-plus two-year 6-1/2 percent notes from computer leasing company Comdisco Inc, priced to yield 35 basis points over the curve via Smith Barney Inc.
Dominion Resouces Inc confirmed it will sell $800 million in five- and 10-year debt through its DR Investment subsidiary and lead manager Lehman Brothers next week.

In secondary action, bonds of Tele-Communications Inc extended their gains following first rumors, then confirmation on Wednesday, of much better than expected operating cash flow results for the first quarter this year.
TCI 30-year debt tightened to a 177 basis point bid compared with a 184 basis point bid, 179 basis point offer late on Wednesday.
Turning to high-yields, prices were generally firmer ahead of what is expected to be another positive read of mutual fund cash flows from AMG Data Services for the week ended April 30.

In the new issue market, zero coupon bonds from Allied Waste Industries rallied as high as 59-3/4 bid from the original price level of 57.436. The $240 million 10-year deal was priced on Thursday with a five-year zero coupon for a final yield of 11.30 percent via Goldman, Sachs & Co.
Finally, CMS Energy Group upsized then sold $350 million Ba3/BB rated 8-1/8 percent five-year senior notes to yield 162.5 basis points over Treasuries via Morgan Stanley & Co.
U.S. Treasury security prices closed higher amid optimism a budget accord could be reached and short covering ahead of the payrolls report.
